units.label: Tactical Roadmap
units.text:
# Tactical Roadmap

The phased twelve-month sequence of the approved platform: signature moments balanced against an always-on presence, every tactic an Activation Card placed by date, channel, audience, message, phase and KPI (key performance indicator).

**The platform is approved: The Stop Line, decided by Kamen Kamenov.**
**The owners and the calendar below are not yet approved; no owner is recorded.**

**Period and markets.** The campaign period is a twelve-month roadmap ending no later than 30 June 2027, focused on buyers in the United States and the European Union, with Sofia as the senior-talent market.

units.label: The phases
units.text:
## The phases

| phase | objective | months |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-Seed | Prepare the proof base, public identity and approval route before The Stop Line is promoted. | Months 1-3 |
| Launch | Introduce The Stop Line through Signed by Humans and direct the market to approved proof. | Months 4-5 |
| Sustain | Keep the platform visible through proof, explanation, partner enablement and senior ownership between launch moments. | Months 6-9 |
| Amplify | Use proof and third-party credibility to widen the story without widening the claim. | Months 10-12 |

The four phases are the year. Inside a phase, each major moment runs Tease → Launch → Sustain → Amplify; across the year the corporate rollout widens the audience Engage → Enhance → Advocate → Amplify.

units.label: The Hero / Hub / Hygiene balance
units.text:
## The Hero / Hub / Hygiene balance

**Hero — signature moments, about a fifth.** About a fifth of the effort is carried by signature moments: The Stop Line proof launch, Signed by Humans founder launch post and earned validation outreach.

**Hub — sustained programmes, about three fifths.** About three fifths is carried by sustained programmes: owner message testing, partner proof pack, technical proof story and the Senior craft story series.

**Hygiene — always-on maintenance, about a fifth.** About a fifth is carried by always-on maintenance: public identity cleanup, proof library governance, the Conversation Management loop, Observatory newsroom and Month 12 scorecard.

units.label: The Activation Cards
units.text:
## The Activation Cards

No tactic goes on the calendar until it is a card.

units.label: Public identity cleanup and proof library lock
units.text:
### Public identity cleanup and proof library lock

**Insight.** The Stop Line cannot hold if public records conflict or claims are not tied to approved proof.

**Idea.** Clean buyer-facing public identity, lock approved proof labels and prepare the Key-Message Table before The Stop Line is promoted.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Internal reviewers and spokespeople use one approved source before any external audience sees the platform.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team has a consistent public base for The Stop Line and no public AI claim moves without proof, owner and limit.  ·  **Targets.** Read public-profile conflict status and proof-label completion at the end of Month 1, then re-read before Month 4 launch.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** public-profile conflict count · percentage of public AI claims linked to approved proof · approval-check pass rate · proof-label completion rate  ·  **Month.** 1

units.label: The Stop Line proof page
units.text:
### The Stop Line proof page

**Insight.** Buyers do not need a bigger AI promise; they need to see what is proved, who owns it and where the system stops.

**Idea.** Create one owned page for The Stop Line showing each approved claim with proof type, senior owner and stated limit; live, unpromoted, until the Launch moment in Month 4.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Visitors inspect the proof behind each claim before they are asked to book a meeting or accept the AI story.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team has a public proof base that paid, earned, shared and sales activity can point to.  ·  **Targets.** Read proof-page readiness in Month 2, launch-week performance in Month 4 and weekly proof-page behaviour from Month 4 through Month 12.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** proof-page visits · time on page · qualified meeting clicks · percentage of public AI claims linked to approved proof  ·  **Month.** 2

units.label: Owner control message test
units.text:
### Owner control message test

**Insight.** Owner preference for control and visibility is a strong hypothesis, but it is not settled buyer truth until owners compare messages.

**Idea.** Test a control-led message against an AI-capability message, both anchored in The Stop Line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Owners react to plain-language options that show visibility, ownership and early risk detection without asking them to become technical buyers.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team learns whether control should lead owner-facing communication before scaling the message.  ·  **Targets.** Read preference split, comprehension, trust lift and meeting intent in Month 3, then use the finding to tune Month 4 and Month 5 launch copy.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** preference split · comprehension score · trust lift · meeting intent · qualitative reasons for choice  ·  **Month.** 3

units.label: Signed by Humans founder launch post
units.text:
### Signed by Humans founder launch post

**Insight.** The human moment makes the AI story credible when a senior person visibly checks, owns and signs the work.

**Idea.** Publish a founder-led launch post that explains Signed by Humans as the visible promise behind The Stop Line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Readers see the senior responsibility behind the claim and are directed to the owned proof page for evidence.

**Desired outcome.** Founder visibility increases while the public story stays inside the approved proof boundary.  ·  **Targets.** Read founder-post reach, response quality and proof-page click behaviour in Month 5, then weekly through the paid amplification window.

**Signature.** Signed by Humans  ·  **KPI.** founder-post reach · engagement quality scored 1-5 against the approved-copy checklist · proof-page clicks · partner reshares · qualified inbound conversations  ·  **Month.** 5

units.label: Partner proof pack
units.text:
### Partner proof pack

**Insight.** Referral partners can carry the story only if the approved proof is simple, repeatable and safe to share.

**Idea.** Build and brief a short partner pack that explains The Stop Line, Signed by Humans and the approved proof types behind each claim.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Partners get language they can use without inventing claims or stretching evidence.

**Desired outcome.** Referral conversations become easier, more consistent and less exposed to unapproved AI claims.  ·  **Targets.** Read partner pack downloads and briefing completion in Month 6, then referred lead quality monthly from Month 6 through Month 12.

**Signature.** Proof before promotion  ·  **KPI.** partner pack downloads · partner briefings completed · referred qualified leads · claim-compliance checks  ·  **Month.** 6

units.label: Technical proof story
units.text:
### Technical proof story

**Insight.** Technical buyers need proof that AI supports delivery without taking ownership away from senior people.

**Idea.** Publish a technical proof story under The Stop Line using artifacts, proof labels and named approval limits.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Technical buyers can inspect the proof route and see where AI supports the work without owning the outcome.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team gives CTOs and architecture owners a credible route into a qualified technical conversation.  ·  **Targets.** Read technical artifact views, sales reuse and qualified technical conversations in Month 7, then re-read during Amplify in Month 10.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** technical artifact views · time on page · sales-use count · qualified technical conversations  ·  **Month.** 7

units.label: Senior craft story series
units.text:
### Senior craft story series

**Insight.** Senior Sofia talent and careful buyers will believe the AI story only if it protects judgment rather than celebrating automation alone.

**Idea.** Publish a recurring Signed by Humans series showing how senior people review work, make decisions and define the stop line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Readers see craft, judgment and responsibility inside AI-supported delivery.

**Desired outcome.** The talent story and buyer story reinforce each other without turning The B Team into a broad ethics platform.  ·  **Targets.** Read series performance monthly from Month 8 through Month 11, with candidate interest and buyer proof-page clicks reviewed after each post.

**Signature.** Signed by Humans  ·  **KPI.** senior-talent engagement · profile visits · qualified candidate interest · buyer engagement · proof-page clicks  ·  **Month.** 8

units.label: Conversation Management loop and Observatory newsroom
units.text:
### Conversation Management loop and Observatory newsroom

**Insight.** Campaign bursts cannot hold reputation if daily questions, issues and market moments go unanswered.

**Idea.** Run an always-on listen, triage, respond and escalate loop for The Stop Line and Signed by Humans, supported by a newsroom that enters only moments with approved proof.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** The team responds with approved answers and escalates sensitive issues before they become public claim problems.

**Desired outcome.** The platform stays consistent between campaign moments and narrows claims when evidence is missing.  ·  **Targets.** Read response status daily from Month 1 through Month 12 and review message consistency weekly from Month 1 through Month 12.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** response time · issue resolution rate · message-consistency rate · approved-answer reuse · escalation completion for crisis tripwires  ·  **Month.** 1

units.label: Earned validation outreach
units.text:
### Earned validation outreach

**Insight.** For corporate reputation, independent credibility makes The Stop Line harder to dismiss than owned claims alone.

**Idea.** Pitch journalists, analysts and named experts only after the proof page, proof pack and technical story exist.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Professional influencers receive proof-led materials they can cite without relying on a broad AI promise.

**Desired outcome.** Third-party credibility extends the platform while keeping the claim narrow and evidenced.  ·  **Targets.** Read briefing outcomes and proof citations in Month 10, then coverage quality and qualified inbound conversations through Month 12.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** briefings secured · coverage quality scored 1-5 against proof-citation and claim-accuracy criteria · proof citations · qualified inbound conversations  ·  **Month.** 10

units.label: Employee advocacy push
units.text:
### Employee advocacy push

**Insight.** Employees and senior practitioners can make Signed by Humans visible if they repeat approved proof rather than inventing claims.

**Idea.** Equip employees with approved social copy, proof-page links and senior craft prompts connected to The Stop Line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Employees choose approved proof-led posts and point audiences back to the owned proof base.

**Desired outcome.** Internal advocacy increases visible confidence without widening the AI claim.  ·  **Targets.** Read employee participation, post quality and proof-page clicks in Month 11, with post quality scored after each published post.

**Signature.** Signed by Humans  ·  **KPI.** employee participation · post quality scored 1-5 against the approved-copy checklist · engagement quality scored 1-5 against relevance and proof-link criteria · proof-page clicks  ·  **Month.** 11

units.label: Close scorecard and message recalibration
units.text:
### Close scorecard and message recalibration

**Insight.** The year only creates durable value if proof gaps, message changes and next-year priorities are named plainly.

**Idea.** Close The Stop Line scorecard, approve message changes and name next-year proof gaps without expanding the claim.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Leaders review what audiences read, believed and did, then decide what proof is strong enough to carry forward.

**Desired outcome.** The next cycle starts from measured proof, not from assumed message preference or broad AI ambition.  ·  **Targets.** Read executive scorecard completion and approved message changes in Month 12, then record next-year proof gaps before the next planning cycle.

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** executive scorecard completion · message changes approved · next-year proof gaps named · claim-compliance rate  ·  **Month.** 12

units.label: The always-on loop
units.text:
## The always-on loop

Underneath the phases runs the Conversation Management loop: establish goals → gather assets → develop proprietary content → deploy across owned, earned and paid → train advocates → deploy (the advocates) → measure → refine — supported by the always-on newsroom running proactive stories and reactive issues management.

units.label: The proof-building order
units.text:
## The proof-building order

Proof builds in the only order that can defend The Stop Line: first cases and proof assets are cleaned, labelled and tied to approved claims; then thought leadership explains what the evidence means through Signed by Humans founder, technical and craft content; only after that does visibility widen through partner briefings, earned outreach, employee advocacy and selective paid amplification.

units.label: The rollout
units.text:
## The rollout

**First audience.** Owners of midsize businesses, led by Elena, because the first job is to prove that control and visibility can make The Stop Line relevant before the AI claim is scaled.

**Then widen.** After owner response is read and the proof page is live, the programme widens to technical buyers, referral partners, ecosystem partners, enterprise buyers, professional influencers, employees and senior Sofia talent using the same proof-first platform.

units.label: Global to local
units.text:
## Global to local

One core channel-agnostic toolkit stays fixed across markets: The Stop Line platform, Signed by Humans signature, proof-before-promotion narrative, do-not-say lines, approval route and global KPI set; local markets adapt hooks, spokespeople, language, local proof and channel tactics, with local targets set against proof credibility, trust, qualified leads, claim compliance and talent pull.

units.label: Client Style Note applied
units.text:
## Client Style Note applied

- **tone:** The client's owned voice is concise, technical and aspirational, with a craft-and-AI contrast at its center.
- **sentence length:** Sentences are mostly short to medium, with one clear claim per line or paragraph.
- **vocabulary:** The vocabulary combines engineering terms with human delivery language: AI development, enterprise-grade software, automation, architect-led delivery, craft, workflow and fit.
- **self reference:** The client refers to itself as The B Team and uses first-person plural sparingly through service and contact language.
- **signature do words:** AI, craftsmanship, enterprise-grade, architect-led, hand-crafted, agentic AI, workflow automations, fit
- **signature dont words:** cheap offshore, best-in-class, game-changing, world-class, revolutionary, full-service agency, marketing activation
- **sources:** https://thebteam.com/, https://thebteam.com/about, https://thebteam.com/services, https://thebteam.com/process, https://thebteam.com/case-studies, https://thebteam.com/privacy-policy
- **long form voice:** Not yet calibrated: no long-form writing of the client's own has been read.
